title: RCMP member lacked drug knowledge, inquest hears
article: No amount of CPR could have saved the life of a man in police custody who had overdosed on cocaine, an inquest in Whitehorse heard on Tuesday.
Clark Whitehouse died after being arrested by police after a high-speed car chase two years ago.

The inquest heard that Whitehouse had ingested more than four times the lethal dose of cocaine- but also the RCMP member who watched Whitehouse eat the cocaine knew very little about the effect of the drug.
The lawyer representing Yukon coroner Sharon Hanley questioned Constable Paul Thalhofer, the arresting officer, on his experience on dealing with people on drugs.

Thalhofer said he didn't have a lot and had never received training on how to deal with people who ingest cocaine. While he deals with people who have consumed alcohol almost daily, he admitted to little experience of people on drugs.
Thalhofer, a 16-year veteran of the force, told the inquest on Monday how he had tried to revive Whitehouse after the man passed out in his vehicle while under arrest.
Thalhofer had apprehended Whitehouse after a car chase, and had to Taser the man three times to get him to respond to commands.
Neighbours who witnessed Thalhofer arresting Whitehouse described him as strained, with a grimace on his face.
"He was trapped in our driveway, where could he go? But he was still running," said Katy Delau, who watched the arrest.
One man said tears were running down Whitehouse's face.
While the subject of the Taser didn't figure prominently in Tuesday's testimony, Whitehouse's use of cocaine was.
"Clark Whitehouse had an ongoing problem with cocaine. He'd been hospitalized several times in the years before his death," testified Dr. Brendan Hanley.

The effect of mixing Taser shocks with cocaine is still unknown. The B.C. police complaints commissioner has said people on drugs, whose adrenaline is already pumping, can't take 50,000 volts of electricity.
There are no experts on Tasers scheduled to speak at the inquest.
The inquest continues with further testimony from the RCMP and the pathologist who studied Whitehouse's body.
